summary.one_liner: Fail2Ban is an intrusion prevention framework that scans log files for repeated failed logins and bans offending IP addresses by updating firewall rules.
summary.what_it_does: Fail2Ban scans log files such as /var/log/auth.log and bans IP addresses that make too many failed login attempts. It bans by updating system firewall rules to reject new connections from those addresses for a configurable time. It ships with ready-to-use rules for standard logs such as sshd and Apache, and can be configured to read any log file for any error pattern. It supports matching IPv6 addresses since v0.10. Configuration lives in /etc/fail2ban, and runtime control is done through the fail2ban-client command.
use_cases: ban IPs after repeated failed logins
protect apache or other web logins from abuse
reduce automated authentication attacks on servers
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL from README; the README omits the URL>
notable: Config-driven: any log file and error pattern can be watched through files in /etc/fail2ban
Controlled at runtime with fail2ban-client rather than calling the server directly
Ships with out-of-the-box filters for common services like sshd and Apache
Long-running community project; original author Cyril Jaquier
caveats: The README says it cannot eliminate risk from weak authentication and recommends two-factor or key-based auth
The init/service script is not installed automatically and must be copied manually from the files directory
Install is from source via setup.py; distro packages are the preferred route according to the README
Code status section is blank in the README
